items.prompt: White to move. Tap every loose White piece. Pawns count.

claims.statement: Exactly two White pieces are loose: the pawns on a5 and h2.
The bishop on b5 is attacked once.
The bishop on b5 is defended once.

hints: Take the White pieces one at a time. Does a Black piece attack it?
For each attacked piece, ask whether a White piece could recapture on that square.
Two units qualify. Both are pawns: one on the a-file, one on the h-file.
items.explain: The pawns on a5 and h2 are each loose: attacked, and no White piece defends them. The bishop on b5 is attacked once too, but the rook on b3 defends it, so it is not loose. Defended is not always safe: that is the next idea.

items.prompt: Black's last move attacked a loose White piece. Find White's best move.

claims.statement: The knight on e2 is loose.
Nxf4 is the engine's best move.
Rae1 is clearly worse.
Retreating with Nc3 is clearly worse.

hints: Which White piece is attacked, and what attacks it?
Running away is not the only answer to an attack. Can you remove the attacker?
The attacker is the knight on f4. Capture it.
items.explain: The knight on e2 was loose. Nxf4 removes the attacker, so nothing is left to rescue. The engine rates the retreats and extra defenders clearly lower.

feedback_by_move.a1e1: Rae1 adds a defender but leaves the attacker alive; the engine rates it clearly worse than Nxf4.
feedback_by_move.e2c3: Nc3 saves the knight but is clearly worse than capturing the attacker.

items.prompt: Black's rook on e8 attacks White's knight on e5, which the bishop on d4 defends. White plays a quiet move such as a3. Does White lose material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on e5 is attacked once.
The knight on e5 is defended once.
After a3 the engine finds no way for Black to win material.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders on e5.
If the rook takes, what takes back? Compare the value of the rook with the value of the knight.
A rook is worth more than a knight, so Rxe5 Bxe5 would cost Black material.
items.explain: Rxe5 Bxe5 would give Black a rook for a knight, so the attack is not a real threat. The engine confirms White does not lose material after a quiet move.

items.prompt: Now a Black pawn on d6 attacks White's knight on e5, which the bishop on d4 still defends. White plays a quiet move such as a3. Does White lose material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on e5 is attacked once.
The knight on e5 is defended once.
After a3 White loses at least a knight's worth of material in the engine's line.
A quiet move such as a3 is far worse than moving the knight.
Moving the knight (or trading on b6) is best.

hints: Same square, same defender. What changed is the attacking piece.
If the pawn takes and the bishop retakes, what has each side given up?
A pawn is worth less than a knight. Defended by a bishop is not enough.
items.explain: dxe5 Bxe5 gives Black a knight for a pawn, so the knight is not safe just because the bishop defends it. Moving the knight or trading it off is much better than a quiet move.

feedback_by_move.a2a3: A quiet move leaves the knight to be taken by the pawn. Engine: far worse than moving the knight.

items.prompt: Black to move. Run the scan's second question. Is any Black piece loose?

claims.statement: No Black piece is loose.
The bishop on d6 is attacked once.
The bishop on d6 is defended once.
The pawn on b5 is attacked once.
The pawn on b5 is defended once.

hints: Find every Black unit that a White piece attacks.
For each attacked unit, ask whether a Black piece defends it.
Two Black units are attacked: the bishop on d6 and the pawn on b5. Each has a defender.
items.explain: Two Black units are attacked, the bishop on d6 and the pawn on b5, and each has a defender. Nothing is loose, so the scan ends quickly and Black's time can go to Black's own plan.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: exf6 is the engine's best move.
exf6 wins a knight for a pawn along the engine's line.
Retreating the bishop at once is clearly worse.
The bishop on b5 is loose: the a6 pawn attacks it and no White piece defends it.

hints: Run both scan questions, and look at Black's pieces as well as your own.
Your bishop is attacked. Is any Black piece attacked too?
A pawn of yours attacks a knight.
items.explain: The a6 pawn attacks the bishop on b5, but White's e5 pawn already attacks the knight on f6. Capturing first wins a knight for a pawn, and the bishop can retreat afterwards. A scan that only looks for danger misses this.

feedback_by_move.b5d3: Bd3 saves the bishop but throws away the chance to win a knight with exf6.
feedback_by_move.b5a4: Ba4 saves the bishop but leaves Black's knight alone; the engine prefers exf6.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxf3 is the engine's best move.
Retreating with Bd7 is more than two pawns worse.
Retreating with Bc8 is more than two pawns worse.

hints: Which of your pieces is attacked? What is attacking it?
Retreating is not the only answer to an attack.
Trade the attacked bishop for a piece of equal value.
items.explain: The h3 pawn attacks the bishop on g4. Bxf3 trades it for the knight; the two natural retreats are rated more than two pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.g4d7: Bd7 loses time and the engine rates it clearly worse than Bxf3.
feedback_by_move.g4c8: Bc8 retreats too far; the engine rates it clearly worse than Bxf3.

items.prompt: Black is in check. Tap every square where the black king can legally go.

claims.statement: Black is in check.
The king can go to g7 or h8.
Those are Black's only two legal moves.

hints: Which piece gives the check? Which squares does it attack?
Could Black capture the checking piece or block the check? Count all of Black's legal moves, not just the king's.
There are two squares, one on the g-file and one in the corner.
items.explain: The knight on f6 gives check and nothing can capture or block it, so Black has exactly two legal moves, Kg7 and Kh8. A forcing move cut Black's choices down to two, and each can be checked in a few seconds.

items.prompt: White to move. Look for a forcing move that wins.

claims.statement: Qf7+ forces checkmate in two.
White attacks f7 twice (queen and rook).
Black attacks f7 once (king).

hints: Which White pieces can give check?
Before you check, ask whether the checking square is defended. The king may just take the piece.
The queen can check from f7. Count who attacks that square.
items.explain: Qf7+ is check, and the king cannot take the queen because the rook on a7 defends f7. After the king moves, Qxg7 is checkmate. The check is only safe because the square is defended.

feedback_by_move.a7g7: Rxg7+ gives up the rook for the bishop and leaves White worse (engine check).

items.prompt: The rook now stands on a6, not a7. Does Qf7+ still win? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qf7+ loses the queen along the engine's line.
Qf7+ is far worse than the best move.

hints: Compare with the last position. What changed about the square f7?
After Qf7+, who can take the queen on f7?
Nothing defends f7 any more, so the king takes the queen.
items.explain: With the rook on a6, nothing defends f7, so the king simply takes the queen. A check is only forcing if the checking piece survives; here the engine line loses the queen for nothing.

feedback_by_move.h5f7: Qf7+ Kxf7: the queen is lost.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a check, capture or threat that wins at least two pawns' worth of material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: No line wins more than a pawn for White.
The engine rates the position as roughly level.

hints: List White's checks first. Then list the captures.
For each forcing move, ask what Black can answer.
None of them wins material. Listing forcing moves first is a way to look, not a promise that one works.
items.explain: No forcing move wins material here and the engine rates the position as level. The forcing-moves-first habit costs a few seconds and sometimes finds nothing; then you move on to quiet candidate moves.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Rh4 forces checkmate in two.
Rh4 is the engine's best move.
Rbe4 is far worse.

hints: Check the checks and the captures first. Does any of them work?
A threat is a forcing move too. What mate could White threaten?
Threaten Qh7 mate and see how Black can stop it.
items.explain: No check or capture wins here, but Rh4 threatens Qh7 mate and Black has no good way to stop it. Threats belong on the forcing list next to checks and captures.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Re8+ forces checkmate in two.
A quiet move such as a3 loses to Black's attack.
Qxg4 is far worse.

hints: Your king is under pressure. Before you defend, check your own forcing moves.
Does White have a check that Black must answer?
A rook check on the back rank comes first.
items.explain: Black's pieces are aimed at White's king, and a quiet move such as a3 loses. But White's check comes first and ends the game: Re8+ Rxe8 Qxe8#. A forcing move beats a defensive move when it is faster.

feedback_by_move.h5g4: Qxg4 wins a rook but loses to Black's own attack (engine check).

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Rae1 is the engine's best move.
Rae1 wins a bishop along the engine's line.
Rxd5 is far worse.
Rxe7+ is far worse.

hints: Look at the checks and captures. Do any of them work?
If the forcing moves fail, look for a quiet move that makes a threat.
Bring the other rook to the e-file.
items.explain: The two forcing moves, Rxd5 and Rxe7+, both lose material. The quiet Rae1 doubles the pressure on e7 and wins a bishop. Forcing moves go first on the list, but the list is not the answer.

feedback_by_move.e5d5: Rxd5 cxd5 gives up a rook for a pawn.
feedback_by_move.e5e7: Rxe7+ Kxe7 gives up a rook for a bishop.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the forcing win and enter the whole line: your move, Black's reply, your next move.

claims.statement: Rf8+ forces checkmate in two.
Rf8+ is the engine's best move.

hints: Start with the checks. Which White piece can check on the back rank?
After your check, how many replies does Black have? Follow each one.
The rook checks on f8; Black can only capture it; then the queen finishes.
items.explain: Rf8+ is check and Rxf8 is Black's only legal answer; then Qxf8 is checkmate. Because the reply is forced, the whole line takes three plies to check.

items.prompt: Study the position. Then two pieces vanish. Tap every square the White bishop on e3 can legally move to.

claims.statement: These are all of the bishop's legal moves.

hints: Follow each diagonal from e3 one square at a time and stop at the first piece you remember.
Pieces can block a diagonal. A piece of your own stops you before its square. An enemy piece can be captured but stops you there.
One diagonal ends at a Black pawn you can capture; another ends at your own king.
items.explain: On the c5 side the bishop can capture the black pawn and stop there. Toward g1 it is stopped by its own king, so it reaches f2 but not g1. Holding these blockers in your head is what calculation needs.

items.prompt: Study the position. Then two pieces vanish. Tap every square the Black bishop on d7 can legally move to.

claims.statement: These are all of the bishop's legal moves.

hints: Follow each diagonal from d7. Which diagonals start with a piece of your own?
On the long diagonal, keep going until you meet a piece.
The long diagonal ends on a White pawn that the bishop can capture.
items.explain: Toward the center the bishop slides to e6, f5 and g4, then captures the pawn on h3. Toward the corner it reaches c8; the other two diagonals start with Black's own pieces.

items.prompt: White to move. List your candidate moves, follow each for three plies, then choose.

claims.statement: Nc5+ is the engine's best move.
Nc5+ wins a rook along the engine's line.
Bd2 is far worse.

hints: Put the forcing moves on your list first.
Does the knight have a check? What else would it attack from there?
Nc5+ attacks the king and the rook on d3.
items.explain: Nc5+ attacks the king and the rook on d3. Black's king moves, and Nxd3 wins the rook. Three plies are enough to see it, because every move in the line is forcing.

feedback_by_move.a5d2: Bd2 saves nothing and loses material (engine check).

items.prompt: After Qxf7+ Rxf7, White is a queen down for a pawn. Judging by that three-ply look, Qxf7+ seems to be a blunder. Does it actually win? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qxf7+ forces checkmate in three.
Qxf7+ is the engine's best move.

hints: Follow Black's best defence further than three plies. Does Black have a choice after Qxf7+?
After Qxf7+ Rxf7, look at the rook check on the back rank.
Re8+ Rf8 and the second rook finishes the game.
items.explain: Qxf7+ Rxf7 Re8+ Rf8 Rfxf8 is checkmate. A three-ply look sees only a lost queen; the reward comes at the fifth ply. Short lines are enough for forcing tactics but can reject a sacrifice that pays off later.

items.prompt: White is considering a4, Be3 and Rac1. Does a three-ply look show that one of them is clearly better than the others (by about half a pawn or more)? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is one of these three, and all three are within 40 centipawns of it.
No line wins more than a pawn for White.

hints: Try to find a forcing line for each candidate. Does any win material?
Compare how the three candidate moves change the position, not only the first few plies.
The three moves are within a fraction of a pawn of each other.
items.explain: The three candidates are within 40 centipawns of each other and no line wins material. Short lines cannot separate them; here you choose by plan, which the next lessons cover.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Rxh1+ is the engine's best move.
Rxh1+ wins at least a rook along the engine's line.
Rg8 is far worse.

hints: Put the checks and captures on your list first.
Look at your own rook on h8 and the White rook on h1.
Capture the rook with check.
items.explain: Rxh1+ takes a rook with check, and in the engine's line the White king steps aside and Rxa1 takes the second rook. The candidate list started with a capture that was also a check.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bh7+ is the engine's best move.
Bh7+ wins material along the engine's line.
Qd1 is clearly worse.

hints: Put the forcing moves on your list, then follow each one for three plies.
A check can also uncover another attack. What does White's rook on e3 see?
Give the check on h7 and look at what happens on the third rank.
items.explain: In the engine's line Bh7+ Kxh7 is followed by Rxc3, which wins the queen. The first move gives up a bishop for nothing, which is why a quick look rejects it and a three-ply line accepts it.
